A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Theory on Mixture-of-Experts in Continual Learning. The main text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–J are readable and support reliable comparison; the appendix content is unchanged apart from pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic linear-regression and MNIST neural-network experiments in Figures 2–3, plus termination-threshold and load-balancing experiments in Appendix A, Figures 4–5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the main experiments and supplementary experiments in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, noisy top-1 routing, expert updates, locality and auxiliary losses, and early termination are unchanged. v2 explicitly names top-1 routing and discusses a hypothetical top-k extension without revising the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic regression tasks and MNIST tasks involving digits 1, 4, and 7. Appendix A retains the same task-cluster scenarios; no additional coverage is evaluated.

E2.justification: The single-expert comparison and the same multi-expert configurations with and without termination remain in Figures 2–3. Newly cited works in v2 are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix A retain the same data generation, metrics, expert counts, and training procedures. The MNIST experiment still uses 100 training and 1000 testing samples per round, with SGD at learning rate 0.2 for 600 epochs.

E4.justification: The early-termination comparisons and Appendix A's threshold-sensitivity and load-balancing analyses are unchanged. The new top-k discussion contains no additional ablation, robustness test, or case study.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging 100 repetitions for Figure 5. Repeated-run disclosures and statistical reporting remain unchanged, with no added confidence intervals, significance tests, or seed information.

E6.justification: Figures 2–5 retain identical plotted results, including forgetting and generalization curves and expert-routing records. Their empirical findings are unchanged; the top-k paragraph offers possibilities rather than new observed results.

T1.justification: The formal definitions, assumptions, propositions, theorems, and proofs in Appendices B–J are unchanged. The added top-k discussion supplies qualitative intuition without a new derivation or formal guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims about theoretical novelty, expert specialization, balanced routing, early termination, and forgetting/generalization behavior.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 newly states that extending the theoretical analysis to top-k routing is outside scope. Section 5.2 suggests that top-k routing might reduce forgetting while weakening positive knowledge transfer, so generalization need not improve. These are limited new scope qualifications and interpretations.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 newly makes explicit that locality-loss computation only needs the selected expert's term because other experts' model changes are zero. This is an implementation clarification; Appendix A's hardware, hyperparameters, data processing, and execution times remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references [44], Yang et al.'s M6-T, and [47], an Evron et al. 2023 entry. These support expanded top-1 motivation and a new statement comparing experimental breadth with earlier theoretical studies. The existing related-work discussion and central positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: Localized additions in Sections 3–6 clarify routing terminology, loss computation, expert grouping, and possible top-k behavior. The overall section organization and most prose, including the abstract, introduction, conclusion, and appendices, are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5 retain their visual content, but surrounding text and equations reflow. Figures 2–3 move from page 9 to page 10, with adjusted spacing and reference placement; there are no added or redrawn result displays.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity by explicitly identifying the top-1 theoretical scope and explaining the efficient locality-loss computation. The new top-k tradeoff discussion is tentative and lacks additional validation. These modest explanatory gains leave the underlying method, proofs, and empirical evidence unchanged.
